input.lyrics:
I remember the feeling, warm but uneasy,
new home, new city, low self-esteem.
I thought being older would somehow come easy,
but each move felt bigger than anything I'd seen.

From familiar roots to something new that year,
I knew every hallway but nobody there.
I went straight home when the last bell rang,
shut my bedroom door and let the phone stay blank.

My dealer answered whenever I called.
That counted as friendship when I had none at all.
I smoked by the window with music turned low
and told myself nobody needed to know.

I found comfort in my room after dark,
with the blinds pulled down and the speakers up.
My dealer knew when I needed a spark,
and I called that friendship because it was enough.

I took pill after pill just to quiet my head,
then smoked by the window and stayed in my bed.
Dropped acid alone while the ceiling turned strange
and waited for something inside me to change.

At sixteen, I thought I had years left to lose.
At seventeen, I had habits to choose.
I don't miss the fear or the things I went through.
I miss being young enough not to know what they'd do.

My first love came through that apartment door.
I had never let anyone that close before.
My mom was nearby, but I lived in my head,
with pills in the drawer and weed by the bed.

We sat on the mattress with music turned low.
I wanted to tell her but never quite spoke.
I thought being loved might pull me ahead,
but love couldn't fix what I wouldn't have said.

I thought getting older would make me feel clear,
but each new birthday just added a year.
I wanted to leave and I wanted to stay.
I wanted tomorrow without changing today.

I took pill after pill just to quiet my head,
then smoked by the window and stayed in my bed.
Dropped acid alone while the ceiling turned strange
and waited for something inside me to change.

At sixteen, I thought I had years left to lose.
At seventeen, I had habits to choose.
I don't miss the fear or the things I went through.
I miss being young enough not to know what they'd do.

I kept the opioids hidden where nobody would see,
took more than I intended and kept it all with me.
I overdosed in silence with the bedroom door shut tight,
then woke up hours later and said that I was alright.

I didn't know what was wrong or why I hated my skin.
I only knew the pills could cut the pressure down within.
Each close call stayed unspoken; I made it look routine.
I kept destroying parts of me before I turned eighteen.

I thought I was weak and rotten, too damaged to explain,
so I punished what I couldn't fix and swallowed it again.
I wanted out of my body, not a story I could tell.
I kept taking what could numb me and then hated myself.

I never called it overdose; I called it getting through.
I didn't know what was wrong with me. I only knew what pills could do.

I don't call it good, and I don't call it bad.
It held some of the worst and the best that I had.
Now when I remember, I can't make it clean.
I hated those years, but I still miss sixteen.

Newark is traffic I pass on the way,
but part of me stays in that bedroom some days.
I know what it cost me; I know what it meant.
I grew without knowing which direction I went.

I WASN'T CHASING A STORY TO TELL!
I WAS SIXTEEN AND NOT DOING WELL!
I WASN'T BRAVE, AND I WASN'T FREE!
I TOOK WHAT I COULD TO GET AWAY FROM ME!
THE CITY MOVED ON WHILE I STAYED IN THAT ROOM!
I KEPT THE BLINDS CLOSED UNTIL AFTER NOON!
I THOUGHT I HAD TIME, SO I WASTED IT NUMB!
BY THE TIME I LOOKED UP, SEVENTEEN WAS DONE!

I took pill after pill just to quiet my head,
then smoked by the window and stayed in my bed.
Dropped acid alone while the ceiling turned strange
and waited for something inside me to change.

At sixteen, I thought I had years left to lose.
At seventeen, I had habits to choose.
I don't miss the fear or the things I went through,
but I miss that old room more than I want to.

I remember the feeling, warm but uneasy,
a new home, a new city, a life in between.
I don't miss that bedroom, at least not completely,
but sometimes I miss what it meant to be sixteen.
